content.title: Rockets vs. Lakers Prediction, NBA Playoff Picks, Spread – 4/18/26
content.text: AP Photo/Jae C. HongUPDATE: Per a Saturday evening report from Shams Charania of ESPN, Kevin Durant is OUT for Game 1 vs. the Lakers due to his knee injury. The original story continues below.The Rockets vs. Lakers game for the NBA Playoffs is set to tip off at 8:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, April 18, with Houston entering as 5.5-point favorites on the spread, via PrizePicks. Saturday’s contest airs on ABC. With Houston riding a hot streak entering the postseason and Los Angeles extremely banged up, which Western Conference club could come out on top? Injuries to PG Fred VanVleet (knee) and C Steven Adams (ankle) left Houston shorthanded, yet it did manage a 52-30 record on the year and the No. 6 seed in the Western Conference.Los Angeles, meanwhile, caught fire in the second half of the campaign to finish 53-29, including a 16-2 stretch from February 28 to March 31.Unfortunately, the Lakers are down PG Luka Doncic (hamstring) and SG Austin Reaves (oblique) due to injuries sustained during an April 2 blowout loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder. Reaves is expected to be out for the entire first round, and Doncic should miss at least a handful of games. As road favorites, Houston is 13-18 ATS.Houston’s offense is nothing to write home about, albeit serviceable. It sits 10th in overall shooting efficiency (47.9%) but 18th in points per shot (1.146). The defensive end is where the Rockets shine, allowing the fourth-fewest points each night (110.0) and limiting opponents to just 40.5 made field goals on average (seventh). The Lakers are the most efficient inside-the-arc team in the sport, making 59.5% of their 2-pointers. They also lead the NBA in overall shooting clip at 50.2%.Defensively, the Lake Show struggle, ranking 23rd in points per shot (1.171).
